story.head: The Blues pile it on the Senators
paras: Dylan Peterson played his first NHL game. Pius Suter got the scoring started for the Blues shorthanded late in the first, and Jake Neighbours made it 2-0 late in the second. Claude Giroux got the Senators on the board four and a half minutes later. Mason McTavish stretched the lead to 3-1, 33 seconds later. The Blues took over in the third: Suter and Neighbours each scored their second of the night, McTavish scored his second of the night on the power play, and Adam Jiříček, in his sixth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Suter, to make it 7-1. Peterson and Jorian Donovan dropped the gloves late in the third. Fabian Zetterlund cut St. Louis’ lead to 7-2 on the power play with a minute and a half left, far too late to matter. There were two three-point nights: Suter with two goals and an assist, and McTavish with two goals and an assist.

The Blues carried the play, outshooting the Senators 26-18, and got the result to match. Joel Hofer made 16 saves for the Blues, and Samuel Ersson allowed seven goals on 26 shots. The Blues improved to 3-2-1, and the Sens fell to 5-2-0.

items.text: The Senators’ three-game winning streak is over.
The Blues have beaten the Senators four straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
Claude Giroux scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 9.
All three of the preview’s calls held.
